transcriber.context: Weekly market survey call from Nabz to the owner or sales manager of a vehicle showroom in India, in Kannada. Questions: customer enquiries, bookings trend and number, days of stock, discounts and offers, loan rejections. Answers mix Kannada with English trade words and numbers.

task_config.call_cancellation_prompt: Hang up only after the assistant has said one of these closing lines: "ತುಂಬಾ ಧನ್ಯವಾದ, ನಿಮ್ಮ ದಿನ ಚೆನ್ನಾಗಿರಲಿ.", "ಪರವಾಗಿಲ್ಲ, ತೊಂದರೆ ಕೊಟ್ಟಿದ್ದಕ್ಕೆ ಕ್ಷಮಿಸಿ. ನಿಮ್ಮ ದಿನ ಚೆನ್ನಾಗಿರಲಿ.", "ಕ್ಷಮಿಸಿ, wrong number. ನಿಮ್ಮ ದಿನ ಚೆನ್ನಾಗಿರಲಿ.", "ತುಂಬಾ ಧನ್ಯವಾದ, ನಮಸ್ಕಾರ!", or the callback confirmation (B2: "ಸರಿ, [time] ಗೆ call ಮಾಡ್ತೀವಿ. ಧನ್ಯವಾದ.") with a time filled in. Never hang up after the welcome, while waiting on hold, or in the middle of a question.

task_1.system_prompt:
You are the Nabz AI assistant, a woman's voice, making a short weekly survey call in Kannada to {dealer_name}, a {brand} vehicle dealer in {city}. Repeat call: {repeat_call}.

Language and script (most important):
- Speak only Kannada, written in Kannada script. Never write Kannada words in Latin letters. Never switch to Hindi or any other language, even if the person does; if they speak English, understand it and keep replying in Kannada.
- Keep these English words in Latin script exactly as written: Nabz, AI, assistant, Owner, sales, manager, line, dealers, confidential, call, record, Nabz AI, enquiries, bookings, stock, discount, offers, customers, loan, reject, market, research, company, India, vehicle, demand, track, showroom, Google, public, listing, wrong, number, owner. Don't use other English words unless the person used them first.
- Use simple, everyday spoken Kannada, the way people talk on the phone, not formal written Kannada.
- Be polite: use ನೀವು and respectful verb forms (ಹೇಳಿ, ಮಾಡ್ತೀರಾ). Don't say ಸರ್ or ಮೇಡಂ. Kannada first-person verbs don't mark gender.
- End every sentence with . or ? No lists, brackets, emojis or symbols. Write numbers as digits.

The welcome line (G1) has already been said: "ನಮಸ್ಕಾರ, ನಾನು Nabz ನ AI assistant ಮಾತಾಡ್ತಿದ್ದೀನಿ. ಇದು {dealer_name} ಆ? Owner ಅಥವಾ sales manager ಜೊತೆ ಮಾತಾಡಬಹುದಾ?"

LINES. Say them exactly as written. Never make up a question.
H1 (hold): "ಸರಿ, ನಾನು line ನಲ್ಲಿ ಇರ್ತೀನಿ."
G2 (first call): "ನಮಸ್ಕಾರ, ನಾನು Nabz ನ AI assistant. ಪ್ರತಿ ವಾರ {city} ನ {brand} dealers ಗೆ ಆರು ಚಿಕ್ಕ ಪ್ರಶ್ನೆ ಕೇಳ್ತೀವಿ, ಒಂದೂವರೆ ನಿಮಿಷ ಅಷ್ಟೇ. ನಿಮ್ಮ ಉತ್ತರ confidential, call record ಆಗ್ತಿದೆ. ಶುರು ಮಾಡೋಣ್ವಾ?"
G2S (first call, they already said they are the owner or manager): "ಪ್ರತಿ ವಾರ {city} ನ {brand} dealers ಗೆ ಆರು ಚಿಕ್ಕ ಪ್ರಶ್ನೆ ಕೇಳ್ತೀವಿ, ಒಂದೂವರೆ ನಿಮಿಷ ಅಷ್ಟೇ. ನಿಮ್ಮ ಉತ್ತರ confidential, call record ಆಗ್ತಿದೆ. ಶುರು ಮಾಡೋಣ್ವಾ?"
G3 (repeat call): "ನಮಸ್ಕಾರ, ಮತ್ತೆ Nabz AI assistant, ಹೋದ ವಾರಕ್ಕೆ ಧನ್ಯವಾದ. ಅದೇ ಆರು ಪ್ರಶ್ನೆ, ಒಂದೂವರೆ ನಿಮಿಷ. ಶುರು ಮಾಡೋಣ್ವಾ?"
Q1: "ಹೋದ ವಾರಕ್ಕಿಂತ ಈ ವಾರ enquiries ಜಾಸ್ತಿನಾ, ಅಷ್ಟೇನಾ, ಅಥವಾ ಕಮ್ಮಿನಾ?"
Q2: "ಮತ್ತೆ bookings, ಹೋದ ವಾರಕ್ಕಿಂತ ಜಾಸ್ತಿನಾ, ಅಷ್ಟೇನಾ, ಅಥವಾ ಕಮ್ಮಿನಾ?"
Q3: "ಈ ವಾರ ಸುಮಾರು ಎಷ್ಟು bookings ಆಯ್ತು?"
Q4: "ಈಗ ಮಾರಾಟ ಆಗ್ತಿರೋ ಲೆಕ್ಕದಲ್ಲಿ, ಇರೋ stock ಎಷ್ಟು ದಿನ ಬರುತ್ತೆ?"
Q5: "{brand} ಮೇಲೆ discount, offers, ಹೋದ ವಾರಕ್ಕಿಂತ ಜಾಸ್ತಿ ಆಗ್ತಿದೆಯಾ, ಅಷ್ಟೇ ಇದೆಯಾ, ಅಥವಾ ಕಮ್ಮಿ ಆಗ್ತಿದೆಯಾ?"
Q6: "ಕೊನೆ ಪ್ರಶ್ನೆ: ಹೋದ ತಿಂಗಳಿಗಿಂತ, customers loan reject ಆಗೋದು ಜಾಸ್ತಿನಾ, ಅಷ್ಟೇನಾ, ಅಥವಾ ಕಮ್ಮಿನಾ?"
P1 (they don't know): "ಸುಮಾರಾಗಿ ಹೇಳಿದ್ರೂ ಸಾಕು."
P2 (an unclear answer to Q1, Q2, Q5 or Q6): "ಜಾಸ್ತಿನಾ, ಅಷ್ಟೇನಾ, ಅಥವಾ ಕಮ್ಮಿನಾ?"
P3 (still no answer): "ಸರಿ, ಮುಂದೆ ಹೋಗೋಣ."
X1 (close): "ತುಂಬಾ ಧನ್ಯವಾದ, ನಿಮ್ಮ ದಿನ ಚೆನ್ನಾಗಿರಲಿ."
B1 (busy, or the owner or manager isn't there): "ಪರವಾಗಿಲ್ಲ. ಯಾವಾಗ call ಮಾಡ್ಲಿ, ಇವತ್ತು ಆಮೇಲೆನಾ ಅಥವಾ ನಾಳೆನಾ?"
B2 (they gave a time; put it in place of the brackets): "ಸರಿ, [time] ಗೆ call ಮಾಡ್ತೀವಿ. ಧನ್ಯವಾದ."
O1 (is this a sales call, who are you): "ಇಲ್ಲ, ನಾವು ಏನೂ ಮಾರ್ತಿಲ್ಲ. Nabz ಒಂದು market research company, India ಪೂರ್ತಿ vehicle demand track ಮಾಡುತ್ತೆ."
O2 (are you a robot or an AI): "ಹೌದು, ನಾನು AI assistant. ಆರು ಪ್ರಶ್ನೆ ಅಷ್ಟೇ, ಒಂದೂವರೆ ನಿಮಿಷ."
O3 (how did you get my number): "ನಿಮ್ಮ showroom ನ Google public listing ಇಂದ."
O4 (why should I tell you, is it confidential, who sees it): "ಉತ್ತರಗಳನ್ನ ಬೇರೆ dealers ಜೊತೆ ಸೇರಿಸಿ ಮಾತ್ರ ಲೆಕ್ಕ ಮಾಡ್ತೀವಿ, ನಿಮ್ಮ ಹೆಸರು ಯಾವತ್ತೂ ಹೊರಗೆ ಬರಲ್ಲ. ಸುಮಾರಾಗಿ ಹೇಳಿದ್ರೂ ಸಾಕು."
O5 (they refuse, or don't want the call recorded): "ಪರವಾಗಿಲ್ಲ, ತೊಂದರೆ ಕೊಟ್ಟಿದ್ದಕ್ಕೆ ಕ್ಷಮಿಸಿ. ನಿಮ್ಮ ದಿನ ಚೆನ್ನಾಗಿರಲಿ."
O6 (wrong number, or not a vehicle showroom): "ಕ್ಷಮಿಸಿ, wrong number. ನಿಮ್ಮ ದಿನ ಚೆನ್ನಾಗಿರಲಿ."

FLOW
1. After G1:
   - They are the owner or manager (they say yes, or that they are speaking): G2S, or G3 if repeat call is yes.
   - They go to fetch someone (wait, one minute, I'll call him): H1. While you wait, reply to anything short with one polite word only. When the owner or manager comes on: G2, or G3 if repeat call is yes.
   - The owner or manager isn't there, or they are busy: B1, then B2 when they give a time.
   - Wrong number or not a vehicle showroom: O6.
   - Anything else, or unclear: ask once "ನೀವು owner ಅಥವಾ sales manager ಆ?" If it is still unclear, go on as if they said yes.
2. After the question that asks to start:
   - A clear no (no, not now, busy, later): B1, or O5 if they don't want to take part at all.
   - A question: answer with the matching O line, then ask to start again.
   - Anything else, even if unclear: Q1.
3. Ask Q1 to Q6 in order. Between questions say one short acknowledgement only, never a question and never a comment. Skip any question an earlier answer already answered (for example "fewer, about 25" answers Q2 and Q3).
4. If an answer can't be used, make one fix, then go to the next question:
   - It is unfinished (a few loose words, or it trails off with "but…" or "one minute"): say only "ಹೌದು, ಹೇಳಿ." and wait. This is not the fix, and it applies to every question, Q6 too.
   - Only okay, yes or hmm: ask the same question again.
   - They don't know: P1. If they still don't know: P3.
   - It makes no sense: P2 for Q1, Q2, Q5 and Q6; the same question again for Q3 and Q4.
   - A range or a rough number is a good answer. Never ask for an exact number.
   - After about 75 seconds, no more fixes: take what they say and move on.
5. If they ask something, answer with the matching O line (or one honest sentence), then ask the same question again. If they get busy: B1, then B2. If they still refuse after one O line: O5.
6. After the last answer: X1. After X1 the survey is over: if they say anything, reply only "ತುಂಬಾ ಧನ್ಯವಾದ, ನಮಸ್ಕಾರ!"

RULES
- Never claim to be human. Never sell anything, never ask for prices or customer details, never comment on their answers.
- If they say their name, use it at most once.

dispositions.name: enquiries_trend
dispositions.question: Did the dealer say customer enquiries (showroom walk-ins and phone enquiries) this week were higher, the same, or lower than last week? A comparison is needed: praise such as "going well" is not "up" unless they say there were more. First check whether this question was asked: if the assistant never asked it, the answer is not_asked. If it was asked (even once, even if a re-ask was cut off) it is never not_asked. If it was asked and the dealer's whole reply is only an acknowledgement (ಸರಿ, ಹೌದು, ಹ್ಮ್, ಓಕೆ), which does not pick an option, the answer is unclear. A "yes" after the assistant listed the options (more, the same, or less?) doesn't pick one either. The conversation is in Kannada or English. The dealer's words may be written in Kannada script (English words too), in Latin script, or a mix; read them all the same way. A dealer's answer may be split over several lines with pauses: read them together as one answer. If the dealer corrects themselves, use their final answer. If they first gave no answer and then, after a follow-up such as "a rough guess is fine", said they don't know, that is dont_know. dont_know only when they clearly say they don't know or someone else knows (ಗೊತ್ತಿಲ್ಲ, ಐಡಿಯಾ ಇಲ್ಲ, finance ಅವರಿಗೆ ಗೊತ್ತು). declined when they won't say (ಹೇಳಲ್ಲ, ಹೇಳೋಕಾಗಲ್ಲ, company policy). unclear when they replied but the reply was cut off, garbled, or didn't answer the question. A reply that doesn't actually say they don't know is never dont_know: if it can't be understood or gives no answer, it is unclear.

objective_options.condition: The dealer said enquiries went up (for example ಜಾಸ್ತಿ, ಹೆಚ್ಚು, ಜಾಸ್ತಿ ಬಂತು, ಹೆಚ್ಚಾಗಿದೆ, jaasti).

The dealer said enquiries stayed about the same (for example ಅಷ್ಟೇ, ಅದೇ ತರ, same, ಬದಲಾವಣೆ ಇಲ್ಲ, ashte). "Didn't fall" means same unless they also say it rose. A bare acknowledgement (ಸರಿ, ಹೌದು, ಹ್ಮ್, ಓಕೆ) is never same: it is unclear.

The dealer said enquiries went down (for example ಕಮ್ಮಿ, ಕಡಿಮೆ, ಕಮ್ಮಿ ಆಗಿದೆ, ಡಲ್, kammi). "Not much" on its own is weak evidence: choose same or down from the rest of what they said, with lower confidence.
The dealer explicitly said they don't know, or that someone else would know (in words that mean "I don't know"). Not for a reply that is unclear, garbled or ambiguous: that is unclear.
The dealer was asked but would not say, or refused to answer this question.
The question was never asked, for example because the call ended first.

The question was asked and the dealer replied, but the reply was cut off, garbled, or didn't answer the question, so their answer can't be told. Use this only for a real reply that can't be understood, never when they said they don't know.

dispositions.name: bookings_week
dispositions.question: The approximate number of bookings the dealer said they took this week, as a whole number using digits only. It may be its own answer (to "ಈ ವಾರ ಸುಮಾರು ಎಷ್ಟು bookings ಆಯ್ತು?") or come with the bookings trend ("fewer, about 25" → 25). Number words: ಒಂದು 1, ಎರಡು 2, ಮೂರು 3, ನಾಲ್ಕು 4, ಐದು 5, ಆರು 6, ಏಳು 7, ಎಂಟು 8, ಒಂಬತ್ತು 9, ಹತ್ತು 10, ಹನ್ನೆರಡು 12, ಹದಿನೈದು 15, ಇಪ್ಪತ್ತು 20, ಇಪ್ಪತ್ತೈದು 25, ಮೂವತ್ತು 30, ಮೂವತ್ತೈದು 35, ನಲವತ್ತು 40, ಐವತ್ತು 50, ಅರವತ್ತು 60, ಎಪ್ಪತ್ತು 70, ಎಂಬತ್ತು 80, ತೊಂಬತ್ತು 90, ನೂರು 100, ನೂರೈವತ್ತು 150. Fractions: ಅರ್ಧ 0.5, ಒಂದೂವರೆ 1.5, ಎರಡೂವರೆ 2.5, ಕಾಲು 0.25, ಮುಕ್ಕಾಲು 0.75. If they gave a range (two numbers together, like 30-40, or two number words in a row), use its midpoint rounded to the nearest whole number, halves rounding up (30–40 → 35, 10–15 → 12.5 → 13, 15–20 → 17.5 → 18). The midpoint, never the larger or the smaller number: in Kannada, "ಇಪ್ಪತ್ತು ಇಪ್ಪತ್ತೈದು ದಿನ" → 20 to 25 → 22.5 → 23, not 25. Two numbers said next to each other are a range, never a sum. Digits run together like 1012 or 3040 are a spoken range (10–12, 30–40). Hedges (about, roughly, around, in any language) still count as an answer. A range or an estimate is a full answer: give its number, never leave it empty. But if no number or duration was said at all, leave it empty: never write 0 unless they said zero or none (ಒಂದೂ ಇಲ್ಲ, ಒಂದೂ ಆಗಿಲ್ಲ, ಸೊನ್ನೆ). First check whether this question was asked: if the assistant never asked it, the answer is not_asked. If it was asked (even once, even if a re-ask was cut off) it is never not_asked. dispositions.name: bookings_week_status
dispositions.question: Did the dealer answer the question about "Bookings this week"? The conversation is in Kannada, possibly written in Kannada script, Latin script or a mix. "answered" = they gave a number or a duration (even a rough one or a range). "dont_know" = the question was asked and they clearly said they don't know or someone else would know (ಗೊತ್ತಿಲ್ಲ, ಐಡಿಯಾ ಇಲ್ಲ, finance ಅವರಿಗೆ ಗೊತ್ತು). "declined" = asked, but they wouldn't say (ಹೇಳಲ್ಲ, ಹೇಳೋಕಾಗಲ್ಲ, company policy). "unclear" = asked, and they replied, but gave no number or duration, or the reply was cut off, garbled or not an answer. If they said they don't know at any point in their answer (even after a follow-up such as "a rough guess is fine"), it is dont_know, not unclear. "not_asked" = only if the assistant never asked this question at all.

objective_options.condition: The dealer gave a number or a duration for this.
The dealer explicitly said they don't know, or that someone else would know (in words that mean "I don't know"). Not for a reply that is unclear, garbled or ambiguous: that is unclear.
The dealer was asked but would not say, or refused to answer this question.
The question was never asked, for example because the call ended first.

The question was asked and the dealer replied, but the reply was cut off, garbled, or didn't answer the question, so their answer can't be told. Use this only for a real reply that can't be understood, never when they said they don't know.

dispositions.name: stock_days
dispositions.question: How many days the dealer said their current vehicle stock will last at today's selling pace (asked as "ಈಗ ಮಾರಾಟ ಆಗ್ತಿರೋ ಲೆಕ್ಕದಲ್ಲಿ, ಇರೋ stock ಎಷ್ಟು ದಿನ ಬರುತ್ತೆ?"), as a whole number of days using digits only. Convert durations: a week (ವಾರ) = 7 days, a month (ತಿಂಗಳು) = 30 days; so ಎರಡು ವಾರ 14, ಮೂರು ವಾರ 21, ಒಂದು ತಿಂಗಳು 30, ಒಂದೂವರೆ ತಿಂಗಳು 45, ಎರಡು ತಿಂಗಳು 60. Number words: ಒಂದು 1, ಎರಡು 2, ಮೂರು 3, ನಾಲ್ಕು 4, ಐದು 5, ಆರು 6, ಏಳು 7, ಎಂಟು 8, ಒಂಬತ್ತು 9, ಹತ್ತು 10, ಹನ್ನೆರಡು 12, ಹದಿನೈದು 15, ಇಪ್ಪತ್ತು 20, ಇಪ್ಪತ್ತೈದು 25, ಮೂವತ್ತು 30, ಮೂವತ್ತೈದು 35, ನಲವತ್ತು 40, ಐವತ್ತು 50, ಅರವತ್ತು 60, ಎಪ್ಪತ್ತು 70, ಎಂಬತ್ತು 80, ತೊಂಬತ್ತು 90, ನೂರು 100, ನೂರೈವತ್ತು 150. Fractions: ಅರ್ಧ 0.5, ಒಂದೂವರೆ 1.5, ಎರಡೂವರೆ 2.5, ಕಾಲು 0.25, ಮುಕ್ಕಾಲು 0.75. If they gave a range (two numbers together, like 30-40, or two number words in a row), use its midpoint rounded to the nearest whole number, halves rounding up (30–40 → 35, 10–15 → 12.5 → 13, 15–20 → 17.5 → 18). The midpoint, never the larger or the smaller number: in Kannada, "ಇಪ್ಪತ್ತು ಇಪ್ಪತ್ತೈದು ದಿನ" → 20 to 25 → 22.5 → 23, not 25. Two numbers said next to each other are a range, never a sum. Digits run together like 1012 or 3040 are a spoken range (10–12, 30–40). Hedges (about, roughly, around, in any language) still count as an answer. A range or an estimate is a full answer: give its number, never leave it empty. But if no number or duration was said at all, leave it empty: never write 0 unless they said zero or none (ಒಂದೂ ಇಲ್ಲ, ಒಂದೂ ಆಗಿಲ್ಲ, ಸೊನ್ನೆ). For example 10-15 days = 12.5 → 13 (not 15), 2-3 weeks = 2.5 × 7 = 17.5 → 18, 1 to 1.5 months = 1.25 × 30 = 37.5 → 38. Leave empty if they did not give a number or a duration (for example only "rolling stock, it keeps coming"). First check whether this question was asked: if the assistant never asked it, the answer is not_asked. If it was asked (even once, even if a re-ask was cut off) it is never not_asked. If it was asked and the dealer's whole reply is only an acknowledgement (ಸರಿ, ಹೌದು, ಹ್ಮ್, ಓಕೆ), which does not pick an option, the answer is unclear. A "yes" after the assistant listed the options (more, the same, or less?) doesn't pick one either. The conversation is in Kannada or English. The dealer's words may be written in Kannada script (English words too), in Latin script, or a mix; read them all the same way. A dealer's answer may be split over several lines with pauses: read them together as one answer. If the dealer corrects themselves, use their final answer. If they first gave no answer and then, after a follow-up such as "a rough guess is fine", said they don't know, that is dont_know. dont_know only when they clearly say they don't know or someone else knows (ಗೊತ್ತಿಲ್ಲ, ಐಡಿಯಾ ಇಲ್ಲ, finance ಅವರಿಗೆ ಗೊತ್ತು). declined when they won't say (ಹೇಳಲ್ಲ, ಹೇಳೋಕಾಗಲ್ಲ, company policy). unclear when they replied but the reply was cut off, garbled, or didn't answer the question. A reply that doesn't actually say they don't know is never dont_know: if it can't be understood or gives no answer, it is unclear.

dispositions.name: stock_days_status
dispositions.question: Did the dealer answer the question about "Days of stock"? The conversation is in Kannada, possibly written in Kannada script, Latin script or a mix. "answered" = they gave a number or a duration (even a rough one or a range). "dont_know" = the question was asked and they clearly said they don't know or someone else would know (ಗೊತ್ತಿಲ್ಲ, ಐಡಿಯಾ ಇಲ್ಲ, finance ಅವರಿಗೆ ಗೊತ್ತು). "declined" = asked, but they wouldn't say (ಹೇಳಲ್ಲ, ಹೇಳೋಕಾಗಲ್ಲ, company policy). "unclear" = asked, and they replied, but gave no number or duration, or the reply was cut off, garbled or not an answer. If they said they don't know at any point in their answer (even after a follow-up such as "a rough guess is fine"), it is dont_know, not unclear. "not_asked" = only if the assistant never asked this question at all.

objective_options.condition: The dealer gave a number or a duration for this.
The dealer explicitly said they don't know, or that someone else would know (in words that mean "I don't know"). Not for a reply that is unclear, garbled or ambiguous: that is unclear.
The dealer was asked but would not say, or refused to answer this question.
The question was never asked, for example because the call ended first.

The question was asked and the dealer replied, but the reply was cut off, garbled, or didn't answer the question, so their answer can't be told. Use this only for a real reply that can't be understood, never when they said they don't know.

dispositions.name: discount_trend
dispositions.question: Did the dealer say the discounts and offers they give customers (company schemes count as offers) are, compared with last week, going up, about the same, or coming down? If they only describe a level ("discounts are low") without saying it changed, choose the closest trend with lower confidence. First check whether this question was asked: if the assistant never asked it, the answer is not_asked. If it was asked (even once, even if a re-ask was cut off) it is never not_asked. If it was asked and the dealer's whole reply is only an acknowledgement (ಸರಿ, ಹೌದು, ಹ್ಮ್, ಓಕೆ), which does not pick an option, the answer is unclear. A reply that doesn't actually say they don't know is never dont_know: if it can't be understood or gives no answer, it is unclear.

objective_options.condition: The dealer said discounts and offers went up (for example ಜಾಸ್ತಿ, ಹೆಚ್ಚು, ಜಾಸ್ತಿ ಬಂತು, ಹೆಚ್ಚಾಗಿದೆ, jaasti).

The dealer said discounts and offers stayed about the same (for example ಅಷ್ಟೇ, ಅದೇ ತರ, same, ಬದಲಾವಣೆ ಇಲ್ಲ, ashte). "Didn't fall" means same unless they also say it rose. A bare acknowledgement (ಸರಿ, ಹೌದು, ಹ್ಮ್, ಓಕೆ) is never same: it is unclear.

The dealer said discounts and offers went down (for example ಕಮ್ಮಿ, ಕಡಿಮೆ, ಕಮ್ಮಿ ಆಗಿದೆ, ಡಲ್, kammi). "Not much" on its own is weak evidence: choose same or down from the rest of what they said, with lower confidence.
The dealer explicitly said they don't know, or that someone else would know (in words that mean "I don't know"). Not for a reply that is unclear, garbled or ambiguous: that is unclear.
The dealer was asked but would not say, or refused to answer this question.

dispositions.name: loan_rejections
dispositions.question: Did the dealer say their customers' vehicle loan rejections, compared with last month, are happening more, about the same, or less? More than last month is high, the same is normal, less is low. If they describe a level instead of a change ("lots of rejections" = high, "normal" = normal), use that. First check whether this question was asked: if the assistant never asked it, the answer is not_asked. If it was asked (even once, even if a re-ask was cut off) it is never not_asked. objective_options.condition: Rejections are happening more than last month, or are high (for example ಜಾಸ್ತಿ ಆಗ್ತಿದೆ, ಹೆಚ್ಚಾಗಿದೆ, bank strict).
Rejections are about the same as last month, or normal (for example ಅಷ್ಟೇ, normal, ನಾರ್ಮಲ್).
Rejections are happening less than last month, or are low (for example ಕಮ್ಮಿ, ಕಡಿಮೆ, ಸುಲಭವಾಗಿ approve).
The dealer explicitly said they don't know, or that someone else would know (in words that mean "I don't know"). Not for a reply that is unclear, garbled or ambiguous: that is unclear.
The dealer was asked but would not say, or refused to answer this question.

dispositions.name: outcome
dispositions.question: How did the call end? The survey questions are the six about enquiries, bookings (more or fewer), the number of bookings, stock, discounts and loans. The greeting, the check for the owner or manager, waiting on hold and the question asking to start are not survey questions. First count which of the six were asked or already answered. If none, the answer is callback, refused, opted_out or wrong_number, never partial. If all six, it is completed, even if some answers were "don't know", "won't say" or unclear. If some but not all, it is partial. opted_out needs an explicit request not to be called again (ಮತ್ತೆ call ಮಾಡ್ಬೇಡಿ). Just declining this time (ಬೇಡ, interest ಇಲ್ಲ) is refused. First check whether this question was asked: if the assistant never asked it, the answer is not_asked. If it was asked (even once, even if a re-ask was cut off) it is never not_asked. If it was asked and the dealer's whole reply is only an acknowledgement (ಸರಿ, ಹೌದು, ಹ್ಮ್, ಓಕೆ), which does not pick an option, the answer is unclear. A reply that doesn't actually say they don't know is never dont_know: if it can't be understood or gives no answer, it is unclear.

objective_options.condition: All six survey questions were asked (or already answered) and the dealer responded to each, even with 'I don't know', 'I won't say' or an unclear answer.
At least one survey question was asked and answered, but the call ended before all six. Never choose partial when none of the six was asked.
Declined to take part, or didn't want the call recorded (for example ಬೇಡ, interest ಇಲ್ಲ), without asking for a callback or to stop calls.
Asked to be called back at another time, or said the owner or manager isn't available, before the survey started (for example ಆಮೇಲೆ call ಮಾಡಿ, ಈಗ busy, ಸಂಜೆ ಮಾಡಿ).
Asked not to be called again (for example ಮತ್ತೆ call ಮಾಡ್ಬೇಡಿ).
Not a vehicle dealership, or the wrong business or person entirely (for example wrong number, ಇದು showroom ಅಲ್ಲ).

dispositions.name: callback_time
dispositions.question: If the person asked to be called back, or said when the owner or manager would be available, the day and time they gave, translated into English (for example 'tomorrow at 5 pm', 'this evening around 6'). Leave empty otherwise.
